g.title: public.clients
g.text: Spa clients (no auth accounts). no_show_count is maintained by trigger from appointment status changes. flags is an extensible jsonb for operational booleans (requires_card_on_file).
Operational booleans, extendable without migrations. Known keys: requires_card_on_file
Stripe Customer id (cus_...). Created lazily by the setup-intent route on first card save. Single platform Stripe account; a future Connect retrofit would add an account dimension here.

g.title: public.organizations
g.text: Tenant root. Single row today; every domain table hangs off organization_id for future multi-tenancy.

g.title: public.staff
g.text: Employees. Linked 1:1 to auth.users via user_id. Deactivated (active=false), never deleted. Self-editable personal fields are guarded by trg_guard_staff_self_update.
Whether this person appears as a provider in scheduling (columns, qualification pickers, slot search).

g.title: public.client_notes
g.text: Tiered notes: preference | internal | health. HEALTH notes are RLS-gated to clients.notes.health.view and must be read through the audited server route (reads cannot fire triggers, so auditing lives at the app layer). Append-only.

g.title: public.client_notes:client_id->public.clients:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (client_id) REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.appointments
g.text: Never deleted — status lifecycle only (booked→confirmed→checked_in→in_progress→completed | cancelled | no_show). Double-booking of staff or rooms is impossible: gist exclusion constraints on the blocked window, which ignore cancelled/no_show rows so slots free themselves.
Start of the FULL blocked window including buffer_before — what all conflict checks use.

g.title: public.gift_cards
g.text: Balance maintained by triggers: created/loaded by a gift_card SALE item, decremented by a gift_card PAYMENT. Balance can never go negative (trigger).

g.title: public.transactions
g.text: The immutable money ledger: one row per checkout. NEVER updated or deleted (no policies exist). Refunds are new rows with negative amounts referencing the original via refunds_transaction_id. All financial reporting reads from here.

g.title: public.card_consents
g.text: Consent records for storing a card on file (cancellation-fee enabler). Append-only: no update/delete policies. method=front_desk_attested is v1; client_signed arrives with intake forms. policy_text is a snapshot of the exact language shown at capture.

g.title: public.client_payment_methods
g.text: Display-fields-only mirror of Stripe PaymentMethods (pm_...). consent_id is NOT NULL: no card exists without a consent record. Detached/expired cards are deactivated (active=false), never deleted — historical payments may reference them.

g.title: public.form_responses
g.text: One filled-in form. answers holds ONLY the non-sensitive answers; anything the version marks sensitive is in form_response_health, behind clients.notes.health.view. No authenticated INSERT policy exists on purpose: a submission must be validated against its version's field list, Postgres cannot check jsonb shape, so writes go through a server route under the service role and the validator is the enforcement.

The subject, when an existing client fills a waiver. Nullable because phase 2 adds prospect_intake_id for people who have no client record yet, and widens form_responses_subject to "exactly one subject". Until then the check requires a client.

Physical snapshot of the consent copy this person actually agreed to, readable without joining the version. Same discipline as the card-consent policy_text snapshot: the legal record must not depend on a lookup years later.

g.title: public.form_responses:client_id->public.clients:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (client_id) REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
